title: Armed Group Responses to Climate Shocks: A Study of FARC-EP Dissident Activities in the Colombian Amazon During an El Niño Year
organization: United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research (UNIDIR), Managing Exits from Armed Conflict project
temporal_coverage: Qualitative focus groups conducted in San José del Guaviare in November 2023 and September 2024, around the 2023–2024 El Niño cycle.
methodology: Two qualitative focus-group rounds in San José del Guaviare with Indigenous people, leaders, youth, authorities, military and police.
limitations: One subregion; El Niño is a proxy, and concurrent political/economic changes confound attribution.

title: Multiple shocks drive Crisis (IPC Phase 3) outcomes in La Guajira and Chocó
temporal_coverage: Food Security Outlook covering June 2026–January 2027; information available through 25 June 2026.
methodology: FEWS NET IPC-compatible food-security outlook using national and local reports.
limitations: Projection through January 2027; local conditions vary.

title: MinVivienda identifica 558 municipios en riesgo y orienta acciones de preparación ante el Fenómeno El Niño
organization: Ministry of Housing, City and Territory of Colombia
temporal_coverage: Territorial water and sanitation risk analysis and El Niño preparedness guidance published 12 September 2026.
methodology: Ministry territorial screening of potential El Niño impacts on drinking water and sanitation systems.
limitations: Risk categories and recommended actions; no household-level estimates or measured service outcomes.

title: Gobierno nacional alerta por altas temperaturas y aumento en probabilidad de El Niño
organization: Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development, IDEAM and National Unit for Disaster Risk Management
temporal_coverage: Joint national alert on May 2026 heat and rainfall conditions, fire alerts, and El Niño probability.
methodology: Government alert combining IDEAM monitoring, recent observations and climate forecasts.
limitations: Short-term alert and forecast; it does not confirm El Niño or attribute individual hazards to climate change.
